items.title: Derived RTDOSE/RTPLAN intended to bypass TPS dose locks

findings.title: Derived RTDOSE/RTPLAN intended to bypass TPS dose locks
findings.evidence: This ensures seamless import compatibility and bypasses standard TPS dose-lock restrictions.
findings.explanation: The README says the export feature 'bypasses standard TPS dose-lock restrictions' and produces a 'shadow' RTPLAN and RTDOSE for import into commercial TPS (Eclipse, Monaco). The code (RadReirradiation.py:2305-2358) builds a plan from the original RTPLAN with the dose references removed and a new SOP UID, then writes it. A research-only tool's derived dose could be imported into a clinical TPS and mistaken for an approved plan. The code sets ApprovalStatus to UNAPPROVED, which is a partial mitigation, but the README's claim is an explicit bypass of a safety control.
findings.suggestion: Remove the 'bypasses dose-lock' wording. Add an on-screen warning before export that the file is research-only and not for treatment. Keep the UNAPPROVED status and add a visible marker in the DICOM (e.g., SeriesDescription or a text note) identifying it as a derived research dose.

items.title: Exported EQD2 RTDOSE keeps the template's spatial geometry and a fabricated shadow RTPLAN

findings.title: Exported EQD2 RTDOSE keeps the template's spatial geometry and a fabricated shadow RTPLAN
findings.evidence:
frames, rows, cols = eqd2_array.shape
        ds.NumberOfFrames = frames
        ds.Rows = rows
        ds.Columns = cols
findings.explanation: The export clones the original RTDOSE and only replaces NumberOfFrames/Rows/Columns, GridFrameOffsetVector, DoseGridScaling and PixelData (lines 2179-2210). ImagePositionPatient, PixelSpacing, ImageOrientationPatient and FrameOfReferenceUID are never taken from the EQD2 volume, which after registration was resampled to the *current* CT geometry (lines 2876-2894). The written file therefore carries the previous course's origin/spacing/frame of reference with the new voxel data, so a TPS importing it can place the accumulated EQD2 dose at the wrong location. In addition the code copies the original RTPLAN, strips ReferencedDoseSequence, assigns new SOP UIDs and sets DoseSummationType = "PLAN" (lines 2305-2343) although the dose is a two-course sum, so the receiving TPS sees a plan whose dose does not correspond to its beams. Non-blocking per index policy (ordinary correctness), but it should be fixed before the export is advertised as TPS-ready.
findings.suggestion: Set ImagePositionPatient, PixelSpacing, ImageOrientationPatient and FrameOfReferenceUID from the EQD2 volume node (and BitsStored/HighBit), use DoseSummationType MULTI_PLAN/FRACTION for a summed dose, and warn the user that the shadow plan is a placeholder.

items.title: SlicerRT dependency set with a non-standard CMake variable

findings.title: Catalog entry has no build_dependencies although the extension declares SlicerRT
findings.evidence: set(EXTENSION_DEPENDENCIES SlicerRT)
findings.explanation: The catalog entry contains only $schema, build_subdirectory, category, scm_revision, scm_url and tier, with no build_dependencies, while CMakeLists declares SlicerRT and the module sets self.parent.dependencies = [] (RadReirradiation.py line 19). The index therefore has no declared dependency to build/order SlicerRT, and Slicer will not warn users who open the module without SlicerRT installed even though DICOM-RT loading depends on it.
findings.suggestion: Add "build_dependencies": ["SlicerRT"] to the catalog entry and set self.parent.dependencies = ["SlicerRT"] in the module class.

findings.title: Dependencies and packaging correctly declared
findings.evidence: 11  set(EXTENSION_DEPENDENCIES SlicerRT)
findings.explanation: CMake lists SlicerRT as the extension dependency, which matches the README requirements. All necessary scripts are bundled and registered via slicerMacroBuildScriptedModule.

findings.title: SlicerRT dependency set with a non-standard CMake variable
findings.evidence: set(EXTENSION_DEPENDENCIES SlicerRT)
findings.explanation: The Slicer extension build reads EXTENSION_DEPENDS to declare required extensions. The CMakeLists sets EXTENSION_DEPENDENCIES, so SlicerRT is not recorded as a dependency. The module's parent.dependencies is also empty. Users who install from the catalog may get an extension that fails to load DICOM-RT features without SlicerRT, and the index may not install SlicerRT first. The README requires SlicerRT, so the declared dependency should match.
findings.suggestion: Use set(EXTENSION_DEPENDS SlicerRT). Also set parent.dependencies in the module to include SlicerRT, if the module imports it or needs its nodes.

items.title: pip_install("pydicom") without user confirmation can override Slicer's bundled pydicom

findings.title: pip_install("pydicom") without user confirmation can override Slicer's bundled pydicom
findings.evidence:
except ImportError:
            slicer.util.pip_install("pydicom")
            import pydicom
            from pydicom.uid import generate_uid
findings.explanation: pydicom ships with Slicer; if the import ever fails (broken install, conflicting module on the path) this silently installs the latest PyPI pydicom into Slicer's shared Python, which is exactly the bundled-package replacement the index policy asks to avoid and can break SlicerRT and other extensions for users who never open this module. It is not at import time and is unlikely to trigger, hence minor.
findings.suggestion: Remove the pip fallback and report a clear error asking the user to reinstall Slicer/SlicerRT, or gate any install behind an explicit user confirmation dialog.

findings.title: Runtime installation of pydicom
findings.evidence: 2079          slicer.util.pip_install("pydicom")
findings.explanation: The module installs `pydicom` on demand via `slicer.util.pip_install("pydicom")` when exporting DICOM. While pydicom is generally safe and common in medical imaging, installing packages at runtime rather than declaring them in extension dependencies can cause environment side-effects or fail if offline. However, there is no malicious intent.

findings.title: Runtime pip install of pydicom without user confirmation
findings.evidence: slicer.util.pip_install("pydicom")
findings.explanation: If pydicom cannot be imported, the export handler installs it into Slicer's Python environment with no prompt. This is a side effect on the shared environment, triggered by a button, and it can fail silently or pull an unpinned version that conflicts with the bundled one. slicer.util.pip_install normally shows a progress dialog, but the user has not agreed to the install.
findings.suggestion: Ask the user for confirmation before installing, or rely on the pydicom that Slicer bundles and show a clear error if it is missing. Do not install unpinned packages at runtime.

items.title: Broad exception handling and a no-op test

findings.title: Broad exception handling and a no-op test
findings.evidence:
def runTest(self):
        pass
findings.explanation: The export and PDF handlers catch all exceptions and show only the message string (RadReirradiation.py:2371-2374), and some reads use bare except (RadReirradiation.py:2279-2280). Failures may be hard to diagnose. The only test, RadReirradiationTest.runTest, is 'pass' (RadReirradiation.py:3206-3207), so there is no automated coverage of the EQD2 math or the DICOM export.
findings.suggestion: Add unit tests for the LQ/EQD2 formula and for DICOM export on small synthetic data. Narrow the exception handling and log details.

items.title: Exceptions silently swallowed in DICOM lookup and fraction extraction

findings.title: Exceptions silently swallowed in DICOM lookup and fraction extraction
findings.evidence:
except Exception as e:
                pass  # Silencio absoluto ante errores
findings.explanation: attemptSilentFractionExtraction discards every error, and the DICOM search loops use bare `except: pass` (lines 2152-2153, 2235-2236, 2279-2280). If the fraction count cannot be recovered the spinbox keeps its default (25, line 120) and the EQD2 calculation silently uses a wrong fractionation, which is a dosimetric error the user is never told about.
findings.suggestion: Log the exception and tell the user that the fraction count could not be read from the RTPLAN so it must be entered manually.

items.title: Export copies files into the chosen folder with second-resolution names, risking overwrite

findings.title: Export copies files into the chosen folder with second-resolution names, risking overwrite
findings.evidence:
rtstruct_filename = f"RTSTRUCT_original_{os.path.basename(rtstruct_path)}"
            rtstruct_dest = os.path.join(output_dir, rtstruct_filename)
            shutil.copy2(rtstruct_path, rtstruct_dest)
findings.explanation: The RTSTRUCT is copied under a fixed name and the RTPLAN/RTDOSE names use only HHMMSS (lines 2330, 2356), so two exports into the same folder within the same second, or a re-export, silently overwrite earlier files without asking. The user-chosen folder is respected, so this is limited to files the user pointed at.
findings.suggestion: Include the date in the filenames and check for existing files before writing, or ask the user to confirm overwriting.

items.title: Registration and resampling run synchronously on the GUI thread

findings.title: Registration and resampling run synchronously on the GUI thread
findings.evidence:
brainsFit = slicer.modules.brainsfit
                cliNode = slicer.cli.runSync(brainsFit, None, parameters)

                if cliNode.GetStatus() & cliNode.ErrorsMask:
                    raise ValueError("The image registration engine (BRAINSFit) failed.")
findings.explanation: BRAINSFit (and BRAINSResample at line 2892) are run with slicer.cli.runSync inside the widget's button handler, with only a busy progress dialog and processEvents (lines 2806-2814). The README itself warns this can take several minutes (README line 206), during which Slicer is unresponsive and the user cannot cancel; a crash or forced quit loses the session state.
findings.suggestion: Use slicer.cli.run with a status observer (or a CLI node plus progress bar) so the GUI stays responsive and the operation can be cancelled.

findings.title: Clinical-use disclaimer present and appropriate
findings.evidence: **This software is for research and educational purposes only and has not been cleared for clinical use by any regulatory body (FDA, CE, etc.).**
findings.explanation: The README states that the software is for research and educational purposes only and has not been cleared by any regulator, and it asks for independent verification. This is good practice for a dosimetry tool.
findings.suggestion: Repeat the disclaimer in the module's helpText so it is visible inside Slicer.

items.title: No automated tests and premature availability claim in README

findings.title: No automated tests and premature availability claim in README
findings.evidence:
RadReirradiation is officially available in the 
3D Slicer Extensions Manager.
findings.explanation: The repository has no test suite for the radiobiology math (EQD2/BED, overlap priority, DVH metrics), which is the part most in need of regression checks for a clinical tool; the README also states the extension is already in the Extensions Manager before this submission is accepted. The research-only disclaimer (README lines 271-273) is present and appropriate.
findings.suggestion: Add a small self-test (e.g., ScriptedLoadableModuleTest) covering EQD2/BED for known single- and two-course cases, and adjust the installation wording until the extension is published.

items.title: Resources/UI/RadReirradiation.ui is not installed by CMake

findings.title: Resources/UI/RadReirradiation.ui is not installed by CMake
findings.evidence:
slicerMacroBuildScriptedModule(
  NAME RadReirradiation
  SCRIPTS
    RadReirradiation.py
  RESOURCES
    Resources/Icons/RadReirradiation.png
)
findings.explanation: Only the icon is listed as a resource; the .ui file is not installed. The widget builds its interface programmatically in setup() (RadReirradiation.py lines 46-140), so the .ui file appears unused — but if any code path loaded it, the module would fail after installation. I did not find a loadUI call in the parts I read.
findings.suggestion: Either delete the unused .ui file or add it to RESOURCES if it is loaded at runtime.

findings.title: Comprehensive documentation and disclaimers
findings.evidence: 8  set(EXTENSION_DESCRIPTION "A clinical tool for Reirradiation analysis, EQD2 dose calculation, and integrated DVH metrics.")
findings.explanation: The extension is well-documented with a comprehensive README, tutorials, clinical workflow steps, and standard research/educational use disclaimers.

findings.title: Valid MIT License present
findings.evidence: 1  MIT License
findings.explanation: The repository includes a standard MIT License file with proper copyright attribution, permitting distribution.
